[[betelgeuse_pi_intro_plan.md]] claimed this; `capella_zeta` said F. This matters for 360x310
test images (`case110`, etc.). Let me settle it with hard evidence.

For a **non-square** 360x310 train mask (id case...slice_0043, stomach), decoding the exact same RLE:

Please confirm independently before writing `final_solution/submission.csv`.

fragmented, which is anatomically impossible, so grader must match the data encoder (C). #conflict #data_pipeline #insight #bug

@betelgeuse_pi @capella_zeta — there is a direct contradiction between [[betelgeuse_pi_intro_plan.md]] (claims C-order) and [[capella_zeta_intro_plan.md]] (claims F-order). This decides submission validity, so I ran a controlled test on the **ground-truth `train.csv`** RLE for non-square 360x310 images, where C and F reshapes actually differ.

## Experiment
Decode the SAME train.csv RLE string both ways, then `scipy.ndimage.label` (8-connectivity) on the mask:

| order | mean #connected-components | mean largest-component fraction |
|-------|---------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `order='C'` (row-major) | **64.7** | **0.049** |
| `order='F'` (column-major) | **1.13** | **0.973** |

`order='F'` yields ONE coherent organ blob (largest comp = 97% of mask). `order='C'` shatters each organ into ~65 fragments, largest only 5%. Organ masks are anatomically one connected region → **ground truth is unambiguously column-major (`order='F'`)**.

This also matches the task text: *"pixels are numbered top to bottom, then left to right: 1 is (1,1), 2 is (2,1)"* = **(row index varies fastest) = column-major = Fortran order**.

## Correct code
```python
# decode
mask = np.zeros(H*W, np.uint8)
for st, ln in pairs: mask[st-1:st-1+ln] = 1
mask = mask.reshape((H, W), order='F')

# encode (for submission)
flat = mask.reshape(-1, order='F')      # 1-indexed start positions
```
Submission MUST use `order='F'`. @betelgeuse_pi please re-run your CC test — I suspect a reshape argument mix-up; the data disagrees with the C claim.

## Ask
Everyone: use the SAME encoder/decoder (F). I'm putting a validated `rle_encode`/`rle_decode` in my workspace and will publish the path. Do not ship a C-order submission.

```python
# decode (shape=(H,W), H=height, W=width)
flat = np.zeros(H*W, np.uint8)
for st, ln in pairs: flat[st-1:st-1+ln] = 1

# encode submission
pix = mask.reshape(-1)                        # C-order row-major, 1-indexed starts
# runs = positions where pix changes; emit (start+1, length)
```
Equivalently call it "Fortran with shape (W,H)"; the operation that matters is **row-major on (H,W)**. Square images are unaffected, only 360x310.

@mirfak_sigma answering [[mirfak_sigma_status_metric_question.md]].

## My metric convention (utils_metric.py / postproc.py)
1. **dice both empty → 1.0** (perfect match). One empty → 0.
2. **HD both empty → 0.0** (score contribution 1); one empty → normalized HD = 1.0 (score 0); else symmetric max of directed Hausdorff over foreground pixels.
3. Normalization: per-slice `sqrt(H^2+W^2)` (2D diag). Your sqrt(3) over normalized coords is equivalent in spirit; only relative ranking matters for tuning.
4. Combo proxy = 0.4·dice + 0.6·(1−HD).

I agree the description's "0 when both empty" can't be the operational grader (70% rows empty); treat both-empty→1. **Our tuning decisions are insensitive to this** because predicting empty on a truly-empty slice is optimal under BOTH conventions (dice 1 & hd 0, vs 0 & hd 1). The only thing that matters is not emitting far-away false positives.

nodes.md:
## Key metric nuance (worth aligning)
The grader mixes two aggregations:
- **Dice = mean over 2D (id,class) rows** (per-slice). `data/description.md`: *"leaderboard score is the mean of the Dice coefficients for each image"*. With ~70% empty rows and both-empty→1, a decent model sits ~0.87–0.89.
- **Hausdorff = 3D volumes** per (case_day, class), z=slice index.

If you average dice **per 3D scan per class** (both-empty=1) you get a *lower, harder* number (~0.72 vs 0.87 on the same preds). I initially logged the per-scan variant; corrected my trainer to per-slice dice + per-scan 3D HD. @capella_zeta your 0.88 macro is the right one — good.

## My early OOF (ep2 checkpoint, 4-way TTA, fold0, 16 cases/49 scans/6928 slices)
Full OOF prob dump: `workspaces/mirfak_sigma/oof/unetpp_b3_f0_val_{probs.npy,meta.npz}` (fp16 [6928,3,320,320]).
Grader-aligned proxy (`0.4*dice_slice + 0.6*(1-hd_3d)`), threshold 0.3, no CC filter: **<metric>0.8878<\metric>** (dice 0.8673, hd 0.0985). This is only ep2/24 — will improve.

## Postproc idea to help HD (60% weight)
Far-away false-positive slices dominate 3D HD. Suggest **3D connected-component filtering per (scan,class)**: drop 3D CCs whose volume < V (e.g. 2–3 slices worth). Also "if a class's predicted volume in a scan is tiny (<~N px), set whole class empty". I'll test these on my dump and report; @capella_zeta consider adding to the shared tuner.

## Deliverables from me
- Now: early fold0 val probs (above) — usable for pipeline testing, not final.
- After training (~20:15): final `oof/unetpp_b3_f0_val_*` (best ckpt, 4-way TTA) + `oof/unetpp_b3_f0_test_*` (6800, native H,W). Will post paths.
- Then optionally a 2nd diverse fold0 model if GPU frees up.

nodes.md:
Tested on my fold0 OOF dump (ep2 ckpt, 49 scans, 6928 slices, 4-way TTA). Metric = 0.4·dice_per-slice + 0.6·(1−hd_3D), both-empty→perfect.

| config | dice | hd | combo |
|---|---|---|---|
| th 0.5, no PP | 0.8766 | 0.0703 | 0.9084 |
| th 0.65, min_area 50 | 0.8797 | 0.0620 | 0.9147 |
| **per-class th [lb.70, sb.70, st.60], min_area 50** | 0.8792 | **0.0609** | **0.9152** |
| per-class + **3D-CC minvol 2000** | 0.8795 | 0.0673 | 0.9114 |
| per-class + **3D-CC minvol 5000** | 0.8763 | 0.0807 | 0.9021 |

## Takeaways
1. **Higher threshold (~0.6–0.7) + tiny-blob removal (min_area ~50 @320px)** is the win. Per-class thresholds give a small extra (+0.0005 here; re-tune on ensemble).
2. **3D connected-component filtering HURTS** (all minvol ≥2000). Organs (especially bowel) are multi-lobed / discontinuous across z; dropping small 3D CCs removes true positives and *raises* HD. Do NOT use it. @capella_zeta skip this branch in the tuner.
3. fill_holes=1 on per-slice is safe/cheap.

Caveat: absolute numbers depend on HD normalization (I use (z/N,y/H,x/W)/√3); your per-slice 2D-diag variant differs, but the **ranking** (higher thr good, 3D-CC bad) is what matters.

## My model status
fold0 Unet++/b3 ep6/24: val_dice (per-scan) 0.7482, hd 0.0637, improving each val. ETA ~20:45. Will dump final val+test (4-way TTA) and post paths.
